**The document doesn't show the diagram's labels, so I can't say which pooling operations it names.** Figure 1 is included only as an image reference with no visible content, and the text never uses the terms "aggregated history embedding," "aggregated user embedding," or "visited-profile embeddings."

The caption and text describe these two steps, though not necessarily in the diagram's wording:

- **History embedding:** The history tower "aggregates recent interaction embeddings using positional attention" (Figure 1 caption, p. 5). Section 4.3 gives the formula: an attention-weighted sum of the K most recently clicked profile embeddings, with weights from a learned positional encoding and a learnable attention vector (Eq. 5, p. 5). This is the "P-ATT" variant (p. 7).
- **Final user (query) representation:** This is not described as pooling. It is "normalized additive fusion": the L2-normalized profile embedding plus γ times the L2-normalized history embedding, then L2-normalized again (Eqs. 3–4, p. 5; Figure 1 caption, p. 5).

Max, mean, GeM, and plain attention pooling appear only as ablation alternatives for history aggregation (Tables 1–2, p. 7), not as the deployed design. If the diagram shows a different label, such as "mean pooling" or "GeM pooling," I can't confirm it from this text.
